prompt: A chain of fitness studios has seen profits fall for two years. The candidate's framework: (1) Membership revenue: members × average fee; (2) Other revenue: retail and personal training; (3) Fixed costs: rent and equipment. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap and should be merged
options.feedback: Revenue and fixed costs don't overlap.

options.text: Bucket 2 doesn't matter, since retail is a small share
options.feedback: Other revenue can still move profit, so it belongs.

options.text: A revenue-and-cost tree is too generic here
options.feedback: A profit tree fits a profitability question. The flaw is the missing cost line.

options.text: Missing: variable and staffing costs such as instructor pay
options.feedback: Right. Instructor pay grows with classes, and it is often the biggest studio cost. A cost bucket with only rent and equipment misses it.

explanation: Profit = revenue − all costs. Instructor pay and other variable costs are missing, and they are a large share of studio costs.

extras.corrected_framework: Revenue (members × fee, other income); fixed costs (rent, equipment); variable costs (instructors, utilities, marketing)
